item.title: Kusal Mendis scripts history, joins Virat Kohli, Steve Smith and Joe Root in elite club
item.description: Kusal Mendis joined an elite group featuring Joe Root, Virat Kohli and Steve Smith after becoming the latest batter to score a century on his debut as a Test captain. The Sri Lankan made history against Pakistan on Wednesday, becoming the first player from his country to achieve the feat. Mendis, who took over as Sri Lanka's full-time Test captain from Dhananjaya de Silva last month, marked his leadership debut with a memorable unbeaten hundred. His knock also placed him among the prominent names in world cricket who have begun their Test captaincy careers with a century. The 31-year-old reached the landmark with a boundary off Razaullah in the third delivery of the 92nd over. Mendis also played a crucial role in Sri Lanka's recovery after the visitors found themselves struggling at 155/4 in 42 overs. He combined with his fifth-wicket partner to put together a massive 249-run stand. With the achievement, Mendis became the 37th cricketer overall to register a hundred in his first Test as captain. He is also only the second player after former England skipper Andrew Strauss to score a century on his Test captaincy debut against Pakistan. The list of players to have accomplished the feat includes some of the biggest names in the game. India's Virat Kohli scored 115 against Australia in Adelaide in 2014, while Steve Smith followed with 133 against India in Brisbane later that month. England's Joe Root also made a memorable start to his captaincy tenure, scoring 190 against South Africa at Lord's in 2017. Other notable names on the list include Sunil Gavaskar, Greg Chappell, Alastair Cook, Kevin Pietersen and Shubman Gill, who scored 147 against England at Leeds in 2025. South Africa's Wiaan Mulder also made history with an unbeaten 367 against Zimbabwe in Bulawayo in 2025. Mendis' century also brought another significant personal milestone. During his innings, he crossed 13,000 runs in international cricket, becoming only the eighth Sri Lankan batter to reach the mark across all three formats. Kumar Sangakkara remains Sri Lanka's leading run-scorer in international cricket with 27,757 runs from 587 matches between 2000 and 2015. Mahela Jayawardene occupies second place with 25,688 runs, followed by Sanath Jayasuriya with 20,966.

item.title: Owono undecided over future following De Miguel death
item.description: Owono has 47 caps for Equatorial Guinea but was not called up during the most recent international window [Getty Images] FC Andorra manager Carles Manso says goalkeeper Jesus Owono is yet to decide whether he will return to football following the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel. Owono was sent off after colliding with De Miguel during a Spanish second division match on 2 November, with the Tenerife forward passing away the following day in hospital. Manso said the goalkeeper, 25, is currently spending time with his family and is "completely free to make any decision" with regard to a potential return. "What we have to do is support him in every way and be close to ​him," Manso said. "We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return. "When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that [he will do so]." Andorra released a statement on behalf of Owono on 4 November, with the Equatorial Guinea keeper saying he was experiencing "the most difficult days of my life". He added: "I feel enormous pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him." The team will return to action for the first time since De Miguel's death on Saturday when they face Almeria in the Spanish second division. item.title: Kyle Busch Posthumously Wins Most Popular Driver Award
item.description: Feb 11, 2026; Daytona Beach, Florida, USA; NASCAR Cup Series driver Kyle Busch (8) during qualifying for the Daytona 500 at Daytona International Speedway. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Kyle Busch finally won the Most Popular Driver Award after his death , securing a record 261,612 votes according to the National Motorsports Press Association. This total shattered previous marks and placed the driver ahead of Kyle Larson and third-place finisher Carson Hocevar. Fans cast these ballots to honor a man who spent 25 years in the national series as a figure many loved to boo. The award was presented at the season-ending ceremony in Miami on Tuesday, where his wife Samantha accepted the trophy on his behalf. Busch had spent decades chasing this specific honor while dominating the sport in every other way. He secured Cup championships in 2015 and 2019 and earned 63 victories at NASCAR’s top level. His career also included a record 234 wins across all three national series. Despite those numbers, the popularity trophy remained out of reach until 2026. Samantha Busch recalled how much the award meant to him before the ceremony even began. “Winning the Most Popular Driver, he wanted it so bad. He would try to rally the fans, and there was one year, I think, either he didn’t see Chase [Elliott] out here, or maybe Chase didn’t come, and he was like, ‘I got it. I got it,’ and he was so excited. And then he didn’t. And so he called NASCAR, and he was like, ‘I want to see the numbers. How far off was I? Was I close?’ Kyle was very competitive, and he took this no differently,” Samantha said before Tuesday’s ceremony, according to Fox Sports . She noted that he had once called NASCAR officials just to find out how close he had come to winning. A Shift in the Fan Vote The result marked a major shift from how fans viewed Busch during his life. For years, his aggressive driving and honest personality made him one of the most divisive stars in the sport . Spectators would pack the stands just to see what he would do next, often cheering when his rivals beat him. Yet he never changed his approach to please the crowd. While maintaining his true character, Samantha recalled that history during her acceptance speech. “Kyle never changed who he was to make people like him.” This win proved that popularity does not always require universal approval. Chase Elliott played a key role in making this outcome possible. Elliott had won the award for eight straight years from 2018 to 2025. He asked his fans to vote for Busch instead after withdrawing his name from the 2026 ballot. This move mirrored what Bill Elliott did in 2001 after Dale Earnhardt’s fatal crash. That year, Earnhardt earned his sole Most Popular Driver award, which was also his first. Following his death, Busch became only the second driver to secure the Cup award. item.title: Man Utd sack manager Carrick, with Pochettino set for hot seat
item.description: Michael Carrick has paid the price for Manchester United's disastrous start to the season (Oli SCARFF) Manchester United sacked manager Michael Carrick on Thursday after their worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign, with USA boss Mauricio Pochettino widely tipped to replace him. Former United captain Carrick led the team to an impressive third-place finish last season, but they have taken just eight points from 10 games in the current campaign and are in the relegation zone. The club confirmed in a statement that it had parted ways with the 45-year-old, following mounting speculation he would be axed during the international break. "After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions," United's statement said. "Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club." United said they intended to appoint a permanent successor "as quickly as possible". - Chaos - Carrick impressed after taking over as interim boss following Ruben Amorim's acrimonious exit in January, leading United to Champions League qualification. He was rewarded with a two-year permanent deal but, hampered by the club's underwhelming recruitment in the summer transfer window, his side have endured a steep decline this season. Carrick has struggled to maintain discipline, dropping captain Bruno Fernandes after he criticised his manager's tactics following a 4-1 thrashing at Champions League debutants Como. And defender Lisandro Martinez spoke out against the club's hierarchy over their lack of top-quality signings. Carrick's final game in charge was a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, after which he stressed he would not walk away. United, however, have decided to act in the hope of saving their season after a paltry three wins from 15 games in all competitions. It is believed Carrick's future was decided on Wednesday during a meeting in Monaco involving co-owner Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox. Ex-Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, most recently in charge of Germany, were touted as possible replacements but Pochettino has now emerged as the overwhelming favourite to succeed Carrick. The Argentine has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, and he also coached Paris Saint-Germain. Pochettino signed a contract extension to remain with the USA through to the 2030 World Cup just three months ago. - 'Legend' - But Sky Sports reported Wednesday that United have "reached a verbal agreement in principle" with Pochettino, who has been linked with a move to Old Trafford on several previous occasions, to become their new boss. item.title: UEFA fine Roma over fan clashes during Man United trip
item.description: UEFA fine Roma over fan clashes during Man United trip Roma have received a €20,000 fine from UEFA’s disciplinary body and a potential partial restriction on away ticket allocations for one of their upcoming European fixtures. UEFA sanctioned Roma after Giallorossi fans clashed with police following an away Champions League match against Manchester United on November 3. Roma fined after fans’ clashes at Man United ROME, ITALY – NOVEMBER 30: Fans of AS Roma show their support by displaying flags prior to the Serie A match between AS Roma and SSC Napoli at Stadio Olimpico on November 30, 2025 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images) Gazzetta reports that the Giallorossi have been fined €20,000 and received a second sanction that could affect one of their future away games in Europe. The European football governing body has ordered a partial restriction on away ticket allocations, reducing the number of tickets available to visiting supporters from 2.5% to 5%. This measure, however, has been suspended for two years and will only be activated if further clashes occur during the probationary period. MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – NOVEMBER 03: Matheus Cunha of Manchester United scores his team’s third goal during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between Manchester United and AS Roma at Old Trafford on November 03, 2026 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – NOVEMBER 03: Bryan Cristante of AS Roma following defeat in the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between Manchester United and AS Roma at Old Trafford on November 03, 2026 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Roma’s upcoming Champions League trip to Paris-Saint-Germain on November 25, however, is already being considered a high-risk fixture by local authorities. Among the matters of concern is the fact that PSG and Napoli ultras are twinned, not to mention that Roma ultras also clashed during their latest trip to France, where 13 of them were arrested for a Europa League game at Nice. The away allocation for PSG-Roma has already been reduced from 2,376 to 1,500 tickets, but, according to Gazzetta, if public security risks increase in the coming weeks, French authorities could even order the entire away end at the Parc des Princes to be closed.

item.title: Daniss Jenkins Explains What Has Clicked for the Pistons
item.description: The Detroit Pistons are off to a 7-3 start this season and visit the Washington Wizards again on Thursday night. When Detroit faced Washington on Monday, Daniss Jenkins earned a spot in the starting lineup next to Cade Cunningham for the first time this season. Jenkins sat down for a one-on-one video interview with WXYZ sports anchor Tina Nguyen . She asked him what has been impressive about the 7-3 start this season. Jenkins said , “I think the biggest thing was shooting. That was the biggest thing. The ability for us to come together so fast. We got new teammates, new guys coming in but we’re all just trying to get that identity back.” Nov 9, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Pistons guard Daniss Jenkins (24) is defended by Washington Wizards forward-center Anthony Davis (23) in the second half at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) What Daniss Jenkins Means by One Common Goal After winning 60 games last season, Detroit lost to the Cleveland Cavaliers in the second round of the NBA playoffs in Game 7. This season, the Pistons are looking for a different result in the playoffs. Even with new players on the team, they still have championship expectations. Jenkins said, “We all are working for one common goal to see how like you can come together and build that bond.” John Collins is one of the new players on the Pistons roster this season. He scored 24 points in the last game against the Wizards. Why Jenkins Earned a Spot in the Starting Five Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff told the team’s website that Jenkins had earned more with the spark he gave Detroit off the bench, and that the staff had talked about improving the team’s starts. Jenkins lined up with Cunningham, Collins, Duncan Robinson and Ausar Thompson in the starting five on Monday and finished with 22 points, eight assists, six rebounds and four steals in 36 minutes of the 122-111 win. Jenkins Is Off to a Strong Start to the 2026-27 NBA Season Jenkins has played in 10 games this season for the Pistons. He is averaging 12.7 points per game, 3.6 rebounds per game, 4.7 assists per game, 0.1 blocks per game, and 0.8 steals per game. He should get another start against the Wizards on Thursday night. One of the most important things for Jenkins is that he is shooting 42.9% from three-point land, 45.2% from the field, and 91.7% from the free throw line. The 25-year-old is no doubt an important piece for this Pistons basketball team.

item.title: Marlon Gomes: “Brazil have always been my second home”
item.description: Marlon Gomes: “Brazil have always been my second home” For someone who faithfully represented Brazil from the ages of 15 to 20, a two-year absence may have felt like an eternity. Between 2019 and 2024, Marlon Gomes played for Brazil’s Under-16, Under-17, Under-18, Under-20 and Under-23 teams. With that kind of history, the path to the senior national team seems natural. Called up for the first time, the midfielder—matured by his journey “in his second home,” by overcoming the challenges of becoming a father at 15, and by the resilience needed to stay focused while playing in a country at war—now finds himself on the team he has always dreamed of playing for. “I spent a lot of time here, going back to the youth teams. I started coming to the national team at 15, so it has always been my second home. Whenever there was a call-up, I was there, along with Andrey. I have many friends I’ve known since the youth teams, and I’m very happy to see them again and to return (to the national team) after a long time, now with the senior team,” he said at a press conference on Thursday (12). Playing for Brazil, the Rio de Janeiro native won the South American Under-20 Championship and competed in the Under-20 World Cup and the CONMEBOL Pre-Olympic Tournament, as well as international friendly tournaments. Marlon Gomes at a press conference in Singapore during his first call-up to Brazil’s senior national team Credits: Rafael Ribeiro/CBF Experienced at youth international level, this time he is one of the newcomers among the 25 players selected by Carlo Ancelotti for the friendlies against Japan and Singapore. “I’m happy about this new project to bring fresh faces into the national team. I’m very happy, and my expectations about returning to the Brazilian national team couldn’t be higher. Now I’m fulfilling a dream with the senior team and being part of this new cycle. I have the highest hopes. This is my first time here. I hope to train well and learn as much as possible from the big-name players, and I hope I can play well so I can come back more often,” he said. A father at 15 A product of Vasco’s youth system, which he joined in 2017, Marlon Gomes became a father at a young age. His daughter Maitê was born when he was 15—a challenging age for someone who would have to balance fatherhood, the daily demands of football training and travel, and the dream of changing his family’s life. Despite the difficulties, he was determined to keep the promise he made to his mother and his daughter’s mother to grow personally and professionally. "I was very young and didn’t have the financial means. When my mother found out, we all cried together: me, her and my daughter’s mother. I promised to change our lives, and not just with empty words, but by becoming a great player and a respectable young man who would make it to the national team. I kept that promise," he stressed. item.title: Barcelona have zero intention of selling midfield star despite growing interest – report
item.description: Barcelona have zero intention of selling midfield star despite growing interest – report According to MARCA , Barcelona have no plans to part ways with fan-favourite midfielder Gavi despite his limited involvement under Hansi Flick this season. The 22-year-old La Masia graduate, for his part, is not entirely happy with his situation, but is also not considering leaving the club in the upcoming transfer window. Gavi going through a difficult phase It has been a difficult season so far for Gavi, who has lost his prominence in Flick’s setup at Barcelona. The Spanish midfielder has found minutes extremely hard to come by, owing to the immense competition for places. As things stand, the academy ace is behind Pedri, Rodri, Marc Bernal, Frenkie de Jong, Dani Olmo, and Fermin Lopez in the pecking order. It has led to him playing only a paltry 227 minutes across nine matches in all competitions this season. His lack of regular minutes even resulted in his omission from the Spain squad in the current international break. Gavi has seen his role reduce this season. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Given his situation, top clubs across Europe are starting to show an interest in the 2026 FIFA World Cup winner. Teams like Napoli and Bayern Munich have been credited with interest in Gavi, while several other major clubs have also asked about his situation. Gavi not for sale But, as far as Barcelona are concerned, the possibility of letting Gavi go in the upcoming January transfer window is completely off the table. Even though he has not played regularly, manager Flick continues to value the young midfielder and the qualities he offers. Gavi remains fully committed. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Meanwhile, Gavi himself has no desire to leave Barcelona amid the growing interest in his services. The 22-year-old Spaniard is understood to be unhappy with his playing situation, but also understands that the season is long and his opportunity will come. As such, he has continued to work hard despite his reduced role, maintaining his motivation and commitment to the group, which has impressed the coaching staff. The midfielder shares a special relationship with Flick, which has not been affected by his current situation either. For now, all parties remain on the same page, and there will no departure for Gavi come January.

item.title: Dortmund CEO Watzke asks Nmecha to refrain from religious celebration
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha celebrates scoring his side's first goal during the German Bundesliga soccer match between Borussia Dortmund and SV Elversberg at Signal Iduna Park. (is associated with: «Dortmund CEO Watzke asks Nmecha to refrain from religious celebration») David Inderlied/dpa Borussia Dortmund CEO Hans-Joachim Watzke has asked midfielder Felix Nmecha to refrain from doing a controversial celebration in the future. “He was with the (Germany) national team and I was at home on the couch. We had a video call,” Watzke told the Ausgerechnet podcast. “If you realize that it’s dividing the fans, maybe then you’ll also have the insight to simply stop doing it. He wants to think about it.” Watzke emphasized that he didn't intend to prohibit religious gestures from devout Christians. "Nobody here wants to forbid anything, nobody wants to punish. We're relying more on understanding," he said. Nmecha's recurring goal celebration, in which he takes an imaginary crown from his head and places it on the pitch in front of him while kneeling, has been heavily criticized, including by Dortmund's fan department. He explained that the celebrations is about "putting down my 'crown' in front of the soon-to-come king and point out to Jesus, my hope and my strength." The gesture is used by the network Ballers in God, which has been criticized for homophobic and queerphobic statements made by its members. Ballers in God is a network of Christian footballers founded in 2015 that records and shares many such celebrations on social media. "When I look at what they stand for: Borussia Dortmund's core values and Ballers in God's basic principles aren't compatible," Watzke said. Nmecha has previously been criticized for religious content on social media, which has been deemed homophobic. He has rejected these accusations.

item.title: At 44, England great James Anderson extends playing career with Surrey after shock Lancashire departure
item.description: At 44, James Anderson is not ready to walk away from cricket. England's legendary fast bowler is set to begin a new chapter in his illustrious career after joining Surrey for the 2027 county season, following the end of his 25-year association with Lancashire. Surrey confirmed the signing on Thursday, giving the veteran pacer an opportunity to continue playing at the highest level of county cricket. Anderson's move comes after Lancashire decided against renewing his contract for the upcoming season, bringing an unexpected end to his long association with his boyhood club. Despite the disappointment, Anderson has made it clear that he still has the hunger to compete, take wickets and contribute to a team's success. 'I still feel like I have a lot to offer': Anderson on Surrey move Anderson expressed his excitement about joining Surrey and said he was looking forward to contributing both on and off the field. "I still feel like I have a lot to offer, taking wickets, trying to help the team win games," Anderson said in a statement. The former England international also highlighted his desire to help younger players develop their skills and progress towards representing the national team. "I also think that I can bring a lot to the team off the field and help those young players who are looking to develop their skillset and go on and represent their country," he added. According to British media reports, Anderson has signed an initial one-year deal with Surrey, with an option to extend his stay beyond the 2027 season. Lancashire exit ends 25-year association Anderson's move to Surrey follows a difficult few weeks after Lancashire opted not to renew his contract. The decision ended a 25-year relationship with the county where he began his professional career in 2001. The veteran pacer admitted he was shocked by the decision but remained determined to explore new opportunities rather than bring his playing career to an end. His departure came despite an impressive 2026 County Championship campaign, during which he claimed 50 wickets. Anderson had also captained Lancashire during the season, making the decision not to retain him a significant development. The fast bowler will now bring his experience and leadership to Surrey as he looks to make an impact in the 2027 campaign. Anderson's remarkable international career Widely regarded as one of the greatest fast bowlers in cricket history, Anderson retired from international cricket in 2024 after a career spanning more than two decades. He finished with 991 international wickets across formats, the highest tally by a fast bowler in men's international cricket. His Test record remains particularly remarkable, with 704 wickets in 188 matches, making him the most successful fast bowler in the history of the format. Anderson also claimed 269 ODI wickets and 18 T20I wickets for England. He made his international debut in 2002 and became the spearhead of England's pace attack across several generations.

item.title: 'Everyone is thinking how is he going to get back in' - Alan Shearer names Arsenal summer signing as the Premier League's early player of the season
item.description: Liverpool v Arsenal FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Alan Shearer has named Ezri Konsa as the Premier League's player of the season so far, insisting the Arsenal summer signing has been so good that nobody has even noticed William Saliba's absence. The England defender has been an ever-present for Mikel Arteta's league leaders, and Saliba's looming return from a back injury now leaves the Gunners with a big selection call. Shearer crowns Konsa early player of the season Alan Shearer believes Konsa has been the standout performer in the Premier League this season after a superb start to life at Arsenal. The 29-year-old completed a £55 million move from Aston Villa in the summer, ending a seven-year spell at Villa Park that brought a Europa League triumph. Speaking to Betfair, Shearer said: "I think the player of the season up to now has been Ezri Konsa." Konsa has missed just one game so far, helping Arteta's side open up a five-point lead at the top of the table. Konsa makes Arsenal forget Saliba injury Arsenal signed Konsa partly to cover for Saliba, who returned from last summer's World Cup with a serious back injury. Instead, the England international has turned that absence into an afterthought for the reigning champions. Shearer added: "I just think when you look at the performances of Arsenal defensively, and look at his performances defensively, we haven't even really mentioned them missing William Saliba. The only time we've mentioned him is in the last two weeks and that's because everyone is thinking how is he going to get back in because Konsa has been that good." Ferdinand warns Arteta of a huge problem Rio Ferdinand recently made the same point on his YouTube channel: "Mikel Arteta has got a problem, he's got a huge problem now. What is he going to do when William Saliba is fit? Ezri Konsa has come into that back-four and he looks like he's been there for ten years." The former Manchester United defender added: "It's a problem but it's a problem that I hope Mikel Arteta will enjoy because he's got two top centre-backs vying to be in the team. It's a good position to be in. I think we will see Konsa sometimes playing right-back." Arsenal head to Newcastle as Brighton give chase Arsenal return from the international break with a tricky trip to Newcastle at St James' Park, with Saliba closing in on a comeback. Brighton, who have won seven of their 10 league games, sit second. Shearer expects them to stay the course. "Brighton could be Arsenal's main challenge to the title this season," he said. item.title: Lindblad and Lawson to continue at Racing Bulls
item.description: Arvid Lindblad (left) and Liam Lawson have taken Racing Bulls to fifth place in the constructors' championship on 114 points, 45 points ahead of Alpine [Getty Images] Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson will continue as the drivers for Red Bull's second team Racing Bulls in 2027. Red Bull had been deciding whether to promote Bulgarian Formula 2 front-runner Nikola Tsolov in place of Lawson but have decided to spend a second season assessing their current line-up Tsolov will be the reserve driver for both teams next season. Team principal Alan Permane said: "I have no doubt that this is the best driver line-up for us, bringing a strong combination of experience and ambition. "Both have demonstrated their ability and potential throughout the season, and we've seen the progress they've made, both individually and as a pairing." The decision to retain both marks a break from the previous Red Bull philosophy of fast-tracking drivers through the programme. Chequered Flag Extra: The Making of Kimi Antonelli Racing Bulls essentially exists to find potential drivers for the main Red Bull team, so the company has tended to jettison drivers who have been given a chance and not succeeded. That's why Lawson, 24, was considered vulnerable. He was promoted to Red Bull alongside Max Verstappen for the 2025 season only to be demoted after just two races in which he had struggled. The New Zealander has since sought to rebuild his career and was much more convincing when he was re-promoted to Red Bull for the Dutch, Italian and Spanish Grands Prix this year while regular driver Isack Hadjar was recovering from a broken wrist. Keeping Lawson on board for 2027 gives Red Bull a known-quality benchmark with which to continue their assessment of Lindblad, who made his debut this season. The 19-year-old Briton has excelled at times in his rookie year but on average has been a little behind Lawson, who has out-qualified him 13 times to nine and has scored more than twice as many points. Lawson said: "We've had a brilliant season together and the team has worked very hard to produce a fast car, which I've loved driving. "It feels great to be part of a historic season for the team as we continue our fight for fifth place in the constructors' championship. "I'm looking forward to carrying this moment forward with Arvid through to 2027; we're building something super positive and I'm excited by what we can achieve together." Lindblad added: "It's been a truly special year, full of new experiences and learnings since the very first pre-season test. I'd like to thank everyone for their trust and support. "I can't wait to get started next year, building on everything I've learned during my rookie season." item.title: How Jason Wilcox dealt with reckless Lisandro Martinez after his public outburst
item.description: How Jason Wilcox dealt with reckless Lisandro Martinez after his public outburst Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick secured a third-place finish and helped Manchester United return to the Champions League. However, the club’s hierarchy ruined all the momentum during the summer transfer window, overseeing a botched-up midfield rebuild and overlooking their abysmal defence. The defeat against Hull City in the Premier League opener teased what was to come, and the outburst following the loss at Atlético Madrid highlighted that Carrick is no longer in control of the ship. Jason Wilcox reprimanded Lisandro Martínez Manchester United’s first real test in the Champions League after nearly a three-year absence came against Atlético Madrid. A goal in the very first minute in the Spanish capital underlined the gulf between United and Europe’s elite. The Red Devils spent most of the night ball-watching or ball-chasing, saw Leny Yoro get sent off, and conceded another. Lisandro Martinez chose to show his intensity off the pitch, as he launched a “blistering tirade” at Jason Wilcox, Manchester United’s director of football, and INEOS over their transfer business. The Argentine was not wrong, but that certainly was not the right place to air behind-the-scenes frustrations. According to The Telegraph , Martínez was fined and apologised publicly and is thought to have been given a serious dressing-down in private by Wilcox over the rant. “Martínez was put in his place,” one source told the publication. The Telegraph added that several people internally felt that the outburst was rich coming from a player who had spent so much time on the sidelines since signing in 2022 and, in the words of one source, was “playing abysmally” and pointed to his contractual situation. Signed from Ajax, the Argentina international is out of contract at United next summer and is expected to depart. Dressing room without leaders The report claims that around the time of that Atlético defeat there were “growing doubts among the first-team staff about whether they could halt the slide.” There was concern that United’s squad was “badly lacking not just in terms of physicality, pace and aggression, but also natural leaders and players with aura and presence.” A week later, United proved their doubters right by succumbing to a 4–1 defeat to Como, who were playing in the Champions League for the first time in their history. According to the report, after this match, it was Bruno Fernandes’ turn to show the world that Carrick’s project is on the brink of collapsing, as the captain publicly questioned the head coach’s approach. He was subsequently dropped to the bench against Bournemouth, who beat the Red Devils 3–0 at Old Trafford.

item.title: Penn State holds key advantages over Minnesota’s defense
item.description: Penn State’s offense is officially fun to watch again. The unit has put together back-to-back strong performances — although it hit a lull in the second half last week — against the Purdue Boilermakers and Washington Huskies . The most exciting part about the scoring uptick is that it has happened without wide receiver Koby Howard . Quarterback Rocco Becht finally looks comfortable playing against Big Ten competition, and it has paid off in a big way for the Nittany Lions . However, they won’t have a cakewalk this week, as Minnesota has one of the better defenses in the conference. It only allows 20.5 points per game, and it is just below the Nittany Lions in terms of yardage allowed, currently giving up 305 yards per game. Let’s compare Penn State’s offense to Minnesota’s defense and see who has the edge. Yards per carry Penn State offense: 4.15 yards per carry Minnesota defense: 3.88 yards per carry These numbers suggest that the blue and white have a mediocre running game and Minnesota has an excellent run defense. However, the Nittany Lions have been running the ball much more effectively lately, and they could pose a threat this weekend. Penn State’s running backs have been averaging 6.2 yards per carry over the last two games. The rushes have been much more explosive, and the running backs are finding yards more consistently in the power running game. This type of balance between the run and the pass could give the team an advantage going into Week 11. Time of possession Penn State offense: 32 minutes Minnesota defense: 29 minutes These two teams have nearly identical average times of possession. This could mean that whoever is able to establish the run and control the game will have a strong chance of winning. We just saw Penn State own the time of possession battle against Purdue a couple of weeks ago, and it resulted in a 31-17 victory that felt a lot bigger than what the scoreboard suggested. It’ll be hard to get to 43 minutes of possession again, but keeping Minnesota’s defense on the field will be key. Fourth-down conversions Penn State offense: 77.8% conversion rate Minnesota defense: allow 55.6% conversion rate The fourth-down battle is something Penn State should always have the edge in, as it converts 77.8% of its attempts. The Nittany Lions have been great at converting these short-yardage situations, and it really helps to give the offense second and third chances to stay on the field. Conversely, the Golden Gophers struggle with stopping teams on fourth down. Getting an extra set of downs when you would have normally punted also keeps your offense on the field longer, circling back to the time of possession battle. If Penn State wins this area of the game, then it can kill two birds with one stone. Follow Nittany Lions Wire on X and Facebook . item.title: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has quiet 4th quarter in OKC's loss to Trail Blazers
item.description: Surrounded by three defenders, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander contorted his slender frame to get by. He took one dribble as he crouched down near the floor. Taking an off-balance floater, he hurled the ball at the rim. It banked in. The circus shot sadly represented his sole fourth-quarter bucket. The Oklahoma City Thunder failed in crunch time in a 118-108 loss to the Portland Trail Blazers . They leave Moda Center humbled at what their glued-together squad's ceiling is. Gilgeous-Alexander finished with 31 points on 9-of-20 shooting, four rebounds and two assists. He shot 0-of-7 from 3 and went 13-of-14 on free throws. He also had one steal. I will say this — before I criticize his night — Gilgeous-Alexander's frustrating games are an efficient 30 points. There's a level of hilarious absurdity there. Goes to show what the standard is for one of the era-defining NBA superstars of the 2020s. Now that that's been stated. Man, the Thunder just need more out of the 28-year-old. Preferably, the playstyle that helped him become a two-time MVP winner. Right now, OKC is getting a bare-bones version of that. It was a tale of two halves for Gilgeous-Alexander. Or, to be more accurate, three frustrating quarters and one strong frame. The shot process has been off-kilter all year. The drives to the rim are way down. So are the free-throw numbers. The 28-year-old has absolutely fallen in love with contested mid-range and outside jumpers. Right now, that's not what the Thunder need. They don't have the luxury of experimentation or have feel-out stints. He needs to be on the pedal to the metal at all times. The first half was the antithesis of that. Gilgeous-Alexander had eight points on 3-of-11 shooting. Yuck. The shot chart painted an uglier picture. It's almost like he's purposely avoiding getting inside the paint. item.description: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images There are eight games in the books — with nine more to go. The Kansas City Chiefs ’ 2026 season reaches its midpoint in Week 10. Nine members of the Arrowhead Pride writing staff each had one vote for our seven midseason awards, so nine votes will be tallied for each award. RG Trey Smith VOTING: Trey Smith (5), Kahlil Benson (2), Creed Humphrey (2) The NFL now gives out the “Protector of the Year” award, so we will too. Right guard Trey Smith is the winner at the midseason point, playing 506 of 510 possible snaps and starting in all eight games. The Chiefs’ run game has been revitalized this year, and Smith has been a key factor in the push up front. Kansas City ranks 10th in ESPN’s run-block win rate (74%), despite two games in which starting left guard Kingsley Suamataia was benched. The Chiefs rank 12th in pass-block win rate as a unit, and Smith does not grade as highly in pass blocking as Humphrey or Suamataia, according to ESPN , but Smith has allowed just seven pressures (two quarterback hits and five hurries) over 307 pass-blocking snaps; Suamataia has allowed seven pressures (one sack, three hits and three pressures) in just 221 pass-blocking snaps, according to Pro Football Focus . The intensity Smith brings is the cherry on top of his reliable presence on the line. He isn’t a perfect blocker, but he’s been Kansas City’s most consistent offensive lineman in a season where the unit’s depth is already being tested. Center Creed Humphrey’s low snaps likely hurt his chances at winning the poll, but rookie left tackle Kahlil Benson deserved some love; he has played every snap possible at left tackle this season. Some of his signings have stunk, but some have been quietly solid. Where he has struggled though is building a consistently good bullpen that will get the team from quality starts to victories. Once he traded for Jhoan Duran, he got himself a top notch end of game piece that locks down games for them, but he still needed some bridges to get to Duran. He had some, like Jose Alvarado and Matt Strahm, but once Strahm was up for arbitration, they moved on from him in a trade. The player he acquired, Jonathan Bowlan, had a strong season in his first for the Phillies. Is there anything more that he can tap into? 2026 stats: 59 G, 56 1/3 IP, 31.9 K%, 6.6 BB%, 1.28 HR/9, 47.8 GB%, 3.36 ERA (3.37 FIP) What went right Bowlan was quite the find this year for the Phillies, eventually becoming their second most trusted reliever as the season wore on. That title belonged to Brad Keller at the beginning of the year, but the combination of the injury to Keller and effective pitching by Bowlan elevated him in the pecking order. He used a hard, riding fastball to establish himself at the top of the zone quite well. Compared to league average, it had more “ride” than the rest of the league, which was surprising. He used that ride with velocity that hit triple digits a few times to get on top of hitters, complementing it with a slider that was a hard breaker down and away to righties, sent to the backfoot on lefties. He did all the things one wants a reliever to do: induce swing and miss, keep the ball on the ground (mostly) and be able to get outs on his own without relying on a leaky defense. item.title: Cowboys vs 49ers: 2 players Dallas should use more in Week 10
item.description: (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fresh off a thrilling 27-23 victory over the Indianapolis Colts, the Dallas Cowboys return home on Sunday to host the red-hot San Francisco 49ers. If the Cowboys want to record their first winning streak since last November, they’ll need to bring their A-game against one of the league’s best teams. Before the two teams square off on Sunday, here are two players the Cowboys should use more in the matchup. 1) EDGE James Houston One pain point for Dallas’ defense this season has been their inability to consistently take down the opposing quarterback. While the Cowboys defense is tied for fifth in the league in pressure rate (32.8%), they have accumulated only 17 total sacks as a team, tied for the sixth-fewest. One change the Cowboys made in the past few weeks to help their struggling pass rush group was activating 27-year-old edge Jame Houston for their last three matchups. Houston, who played just 13 defensive snaps before Dallas’ Week 8 matchup against Arizona, made a big impact in his first outing with increased opportunities. In that game against the Cardinals, Houston recorded two pressures and a sack on just 11 pass-rush snaps. The former sixth-round pick had a 27.3% win percentage in that contest, the highest of any Cowboys defender, to go with a PRP of 13.6. After an impressive performance, Dallas rewarded him with more chances against the Colts. Houston played a season-high 31 defensive snaps with 18 pass-rush opportunities. While the 27-year-old couldn’t quite replicate his pass-rush success from a week prior, he recorded a 69.3 pass-rush grade on true pass sets, with a 12.5% TPS win percentage. If the Cowboys want the best chance to improve their pass rush, they need to keep increasing Houston’s usage on defense. Dallas should give Houston some of Donovan Ezeiruaku and Von Miller’s snaps to see if he can continue his upward trajectory. 2) S Alijah Clark The Cowboys defense got some unfortunate news after Sunday’s win. Safety P.J. Locke suffered a concussion and has already been ruled out for this week’s matchup against the 49ers. If the Cowboys are going to continue to play Caleb Downs primarily in the slot, Downs played 35 snaps there on Sunday; they’ll need someone to replace Locke as their second primary safety. Dallas’ coaching staff has shown an affinity for giving Markquese Bell chances when they had injuries to both starting safeties early in the year, but given how poorly Bell has performed, it’s time to give Alijah Clark the nod. Clark played 40 defensive snaps against the Eagles a few weeks back, allowing just one catch for nine yards in coverage. While Clark may not be as sure of a tackler as Bell, he is without a doubt more skilled in coverage. Dallas should give Clark the job to start alongside Malik Hooker and see if he can perform better than Bell has.

item.title: Yankees Birthday of the Day: Carl Mays
item.description: (Original Caption) Carl Mays, New York Yankees Pitcher in action. Carl Mays probably would’ve enjoyed one single entry in the annals of baseball lore that doesn’t mention the most regrettable of the thousands of pitches that he threw across a 15-year career that saw him capture four World Series titles. Alas, even on his 135th birthday, we cannot grant that wish. No matter how great he was on the mound, his story will always be tied to that of Cleveland shortstop Ray Chapman. That’s just how it is. Carl William Mays Born: November 12, 1891 (Liberty, KY) Died: April 4, 1971 (El Cajon, CA) Yankees Tenure : 1919-23 Mays was born in Kentucky to a Methodist minister named William Mays (ah, baseball coincidences), who died when Carl was just 12 years old. The family had moved to Missouri by then, but they packed up again after William’s death, en route to Kingfisher, Oklahoma. It was a sad time for Mays’ family, but he did get the opportunity to meet his cousin, John Long. He was a catcher, and he introduced Mays to the game. Pitching to Long, Mays developed the raw skills to attract the notice of traveling teams. At the age of 20, Mays signed with the Class D Western Tri-State League’s Boise Irrigators, who offered him $90 per month.
